name: Tabletop exercises
source: invented example written for calibration, October 2026
agreedBy: Proposed by agentic-rig, to be confirmed by Anthony Stevenson

input.delivery: We run incident response tabletop exercises for mid-sized hospitals. One exercise is a one-day on-site session led by one of our facilitators, with about two days of preparation and one day of write-up. Each facilitator runs one exercise a week, forty weeks a year. We have three facilitators and thirty hospital customers.
input.pricing: Priced per exercise at 9,500 CAD. A three exercise programme is 25,000 CAD. No retainer, no subscription.
input.cost: A facilitator costs us about 140,000 CAD a year fully loaded. Preparation is mostly re-used templates now, so a new facilitator reaches full speed in six weeks. Margin per exercise is about 60 percent and has held at that level for two years; adding a facilitator adds the same margin again, no better.
input.renewal: About half of hospitals book a second exercise within eighteen months, usually the same size. Two of thirty have bought a programme. We are building a self-serve scenario library that hospitals could run themselves between exercises, priced as an annual licence, with two pilot customers using it now.

note: The unit is a facilitator day (mostly people, with templates cutting preparation), one facilitator serves one hospital at a time, margin holds at 60 percent but does not improve with volume, about half of customers rebook, value per unit grows a little through the programme, and the scenario library is a started lever with two pilots. The ceiling computes from one exercise a week at 9,500 CAD over forty weeks: 380,000 CAD per head per year. Weighted score 52, grade 3.
